test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user cannot access the Links tab on a project detail page
test_cases.steps: 1. Open a project detail URL (e.g. /projects/PROJ-1/) without being logged in.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page. The Links tab and its content are not accessible.

test_cases.scenario: Links tab is visible to all authenticated users regardless of permissions
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as any authenticated user.
2. Open any project detail page.
3. Observe the tab bar.
test_cases.expected: The 'Links' tab (with a link icon) is visible in the project tab bar. The tab can be clicked and the Links panel is displayed.

test_cases.scenario: Add Link button is only visible to users with 'projects.add_projectlink' permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with 'projects.add_projectlink' permission.
2. Open a project detail page and click the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: An 'Add Link' button is visible above the links table.

test_cases.scenario: Add Link button is not visible to users without 'projects.add_projectlink'
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without 'projects.add_projectlink' permission.
2. Open a project detail page and click the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: No 'Add Link' button is visible. The links table is shown in read-only mode.

test_cases.scenario: Edit and Delete row actions are only visible to users with 'projects.change_projectlink'
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with 'projects.change_projectlink' permission.
2. Open the Links tab on a project that has at least one link.
3. Observe the row action controls.
test_cases.expected: Each table row shows an Edit action and a Delete action.

test_cases.scenario: Edit and Delete row actions are not present for users without 'projects.change_projectlink'
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without 'projects.change_projectlink' permission.
2. Open the Links tab on a project with links.
test_cases.expected: No edit or delete controls are visible in the table rows. Rows are read-only.

test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated POST to the links API returns 401
test_cases.steps: 1. Send a POST request to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/ without an Authorization header.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 401 Unauthorized is returned. No link is created.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user without 'projects.add_projectlink' receives 403 on POST
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without 'projects.add_projectlink'.
2. Send an authenticated POST request to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/ with a valid payload.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned. No link is created.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user without 'projects.change_projectlink' receives 403 on PATCH
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without 'projects.change_projectlink'.
2. Send an authenticated PATCH request to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/PROJLNK-1/ with a valid payload.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned. The link is not modified.

test_cases.scenario: Authenticated user without 'projects.delete_projectlink' receives 403 on DELETE
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without 'projects.delete_projectlink'.
2. Send an authenticated DELETE request to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/PROJLNK-1/.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned. The link is not deleted.

test_cases.scenario: Links tab shows all links for the project in a data table
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project that has two or more links.
2. Click the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: All links for the project are shown in the data table. Each row displays the link title and its URL as a clickable anchor.

test_cases.scenario: Empty state message is shown when a project has no links
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project that has no links.
2. Click the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: The table shows an empty-state message (e.g. 'No links found.'). No rows are displayed.

test_cases.scenario: Links are displayed in alphabetical order by title
test_cases.steps:
1. Add three links with titles 'Zebra', 'Alpha', and 'Mango' to a project.
2. Open the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: The table rows appear in the order: Alpha, Mango, Zebra — sorted alphabetically by title.

test_cases.scenario: The URL column renders the URL as a clickable link opening in a new tab
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a project with at least one link.
2. Click the URL displayed in the table row.
test_cases.expected: A new browser tab opens navigating to the linked URL. The original page remains open.

test_cases.scenario: Links tab data is loaded lazily — the API is not called until the tab is first activated
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page (defaulting to the General tab).
2. Check network requests.
3. Click the Links tab.
4. Check network requests again.
test_cases.expected: No API call to /api/v1/projects/.../links/ is made when the page first loads. The call is made only when the Links tab is clicked for the first time.

test_cases.scenario: Switching away from the Links tab and back does not reload the data from the API
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Links tab — data loads.
2. Click a different tab (e.g. General).
3. Click the Links tab again.
test_cases.expected: The previously loaded links are shown immediately. No additional API request is made on the second activation of the Links tab.

test_cases.scenario: The project_code field in the API response matches the project being viewed
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project with code PROJ-5.
2. Click the Links tab.
3. Inspect the API response for /api/v1/projects/PROJ-5/links/.
test_cases.expected: Every item in the response has 'project_code': 'PROJ-5'. No links from other projects are included.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking 'Add Link' opens the create drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a project.
2. Click the 'Add Link' button.
test_cases.expected: A slide-in drawer opens with a 'Title' text field and a 'URL' website field, and a primary action button to save.

test_cases.scenario: Submitting a valid title and URL creates the link and refreshes the table
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter 'Project Wiki' in the Title field.
3. Enter 'https://wiki.example.com' in the URL field.
4. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. 'Project Wiki' appears as a new row in the links table with the provided URL.

test_cases.scenario: Title field is required — saving without a title shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Leave the Title field empty.
3. Enter a valid URL.
4. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the Title field. The drawer remains open. No API call is made. No link is created.

test_cases.scenario: URL field is required — saving without a URL shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter a title.
3. Leave the URL field empty.
4. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the URL field. The drawer remains open. No API call is made. No link is created.

test_cases.scenario: Entering an invalid URL format shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter 'Project Docs' in the Title field.
3. Enter 'not-a-url' in the URL field.
4. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the URL field ('Enter a valid URL.' or similar). The drawer remains open. No link is created.

test_cases.scenario: Title field enforces a maximum length of 200 characters
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter a title exceeding 200 characters.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the Title field indicating the maximum length has been exceeded. The link is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Duplicate title on the same project is rejected with a clear error message
test_cases.steps:
1. Add a link with title 'Jira Board' to a project.
2. Open the Add Link drawer again.
3. Enter 'Jira Board' in the Title field with a different URL.
4. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: An error toast or inline error appears indicating a link with this title already exists for this project. The drawer remains open. No duplicate link is created.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the Add Link drawer discards all input
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter a title and URL.
3. Close or cancel the drawer.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No link is added to the table. The entered values are not saved.

test_cases.scenario: Save button shows a loading/busy state while the API request is in-flight
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter a valid title and URL.
3. Click the save button on a slow connection and observe the button before a response arrives.
test_cases.expected: The save button becomes disabled and shows a loading indicator (e.g. 'Saving…'). It cannot be clicked again while the request is pending.

test_cases.scenario: Same title can be used on a different project without error
test_cases.steps:
1. Add a link titled 'Design Specs' to Project A.
2. Open Project B's Links tab.
3. Add a link titled 'Design Specs' to Project B.
test_cases.expected: The link is created successfully on Project B. The title uniqueness constraint applies per project only.

test_cases.scenario: Re-opening the Add Link drawer after a successful creation shows a blank form
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a link via the drawer.
2. Click 'Add Link' again to open the drawer.
test_cases.expected: The Title and URL fields are empty. The form is reset and ready for a new entry.

test_cases.scenario: Server-side error during creation shows an error toast and keeps the drawer open
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer with valid data.
2. Simulate a server error (e.g. block the API request in dev tools).
3. Click save.
test_cases.expected: An error toast appears. The save button is restored to its enabled state. The drawer remains open with the entered values intact so the user can retry.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Edit action on a row opens the edit drawer pre-populated with current values
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a project with at least one link.
2. Click the Edit action on a row.
test_cases.expected: A slide-in edit drawer opens. The Title field shows the link's current title. The URL field shows the link's current URL.

test_cases.scenario: Submitting valid changes updates the link and refreshes the table
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a link.
2. Change the Title to 'Updated Title'.
3. Click the save button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The table row is updated with 'Updated Title'.

test_cases.scenario: Updating the URL to a new valid URL saves successfully
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a link.
2. Change the URL to 'https://new-destination.com'.
3. Click save.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The table row now shows the new URL as a clickable link.

test_cases.scenario: Keeping the same title in the edit drawer does not trigger a duplicate error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a link.
2. Do not change the Title.
3. Change the URL.
4. Click save.
test_cases.expected: The link is updated without any duplicate title error. Only the URL changes.

test_cases.scenario: Changing a title to one already used by another link on the same project is rejected
test_cases.steps:
1. A project has two links: 'Wiki' and 'Jira'.
2. Open the edit drawer for 'Wiki'.
3. Change the title to 'Jira'.
4. Click save.
test_cases.expected: An error is returned indicating the title 'Jira' already exists for this project. The link is not updated.

test_cases.scenario: Entering an invalid URL in the edit drawer shows a validation error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a link.
2. Change the URL to 'plaintext' (no protocol).
3. Click save.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the URL field. The drawer remains open. The link is not updated.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the edit drawer discards changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a link.
2. Modify the title.
3. Close or cancel the drawer.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The table still shows the original title. No changes were saved.

test_cases.scenario: Save button shows a busy state while the PATCH request is in-flight
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Make a change and click save on a slow connection.
3. Observe the save button before the response arrives.
test_cases.expected: The save button becomes disabled and shows a loading indicator while the request is pending.

test_cases.scenario: Submitting the edit drawer with no changes made still completes without error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a link.
2. Click save immediately without changing any field.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes with a success response. The link values remain unchanged in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Server-side error during update shows an error toast and keeps the drawer open
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer with a valid change.
2. Block the API request in dev tools.
3. Click save.
test_cases.expected: An error toast appears. The save button is restored. The drawer remains open with the modified values intact.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking the Delete action opens a confirmation modal
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a project with at least one link.
2. Click the Delete action on a row.
test_cases.expected: A confirmation modal opens showing the link title and asking the user to confirm deletion. A typed-confirmation field or a confirm button is present.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deletion removes the link and refreshes the table
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Delete action on a link row.
2. Confirm the deletion in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The deleted link no longer appears in the table. If it was the only link, the empty-state message is shown.

test_cases.scenario: Dismissing the confirmation modal does not delete the link
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Delete action on a link row.
2. Cancel or close the confirmation modal without confirming.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The link remains in the table unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Attempting to delete a link that was already removed (concurrent session) returns a 404 error
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the delete confirmation modal for a link.
2. In a separate session, delete the same link.
3. Confirm deletion in the first session.
test_cases.expected: An error toast is shown indicating the link was not found. The table refreshes and the link is not present.

test_cases.scenario: Deleting a link does not affect other links on the same project
test_cases.steps:
1. A project has three links: A, B, and C.
2. Delete link B.
test_cases.expected: Links A and C remain in the table. Only link B is removed.

test_cases.scenario: URL without a valid scheme (http/https) is rejected on creation
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter 'example.com' (no protocol) in the URL field.
3. Click save.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the URL field. The link is not created.

test_cases.scenario: URL with 'http://' scheme is accepted and stored
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter a URL beginning with 'http://' (e.g. 'http://intranet.example.com').
3. Click save.
test_cases.expected: The link is created and the URL is stored as entered. The link is clickable in the table.

test_cases.scenario: URL with 'https://' scheme is accepted and stored
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer.
2. Enter a URL beginning with 'https://' (e.g. 'https://secure.example.com/path').
3. Click save.
test_cases.expected: The link is created. The full URL (including path) is shown in the table and opens correctly.

test_cases.scenario: URL in the table row opens in a new browser tab with rel='noopener noreferrer'
test_cases.steps:
1. View a link row in the Links table.
2. Inspect the anchor element for the URL.
3. Click the link.
test_cases.expected: The link has target='_blank' and rel='noopener noreferrer'. Clicking it opens the URL in a new tab without navigating away from the project detail page.

test_cases.scenario: URL containing query parameters and fragments is accepted and displayed correctly
test_cases.steps:
1. Add a link with URL 'https://example.com/page?tab=overview#section-2'.
2. View the row in the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: The full URL including query parameters and fragment is stored and displayed without truncation. Clicking it navigates to the full URL.

test_cases.scenario: A very long URL (up to 500 characters) is accepted and stored in full
test_cases.steps:
1. Construct a valid URL that is exactly 500 characters long (e.g. https://example.com/ followed by a long path).
2. Add it as a link URL.
3. Save.
test_cases.expected: The link is created successfully. The URL is stored in full. The display may truncate visually but the full URL is accessible on click.

test_cases.scenario: A URL exceeding 500 characters is rejected by the API
test_cases.steps: 1. Send a POST to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/ with a URL field longer than 500 characters.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 400 Bad Request is returned. The link is not created.

test_cases.scenario: Links tab loads and renders all links within an acceptable time
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project with 20+ links.
2. Click the Links tab.
3. Measure the time from tab click to all rows being visible.
test_cases.expected: The links table renders with all rows within 2 seconds on a standard connection. No loading spinner persists beyond that time.

test_cases.scenario: Create and edit drawers open instantly without delay
test_cases.steps:
1. Click 'Add Link'.
2. Measure the time until the drawer is fully open and the fields are focusable.
test_cases.expected: The drawer opens within 300ms. There is no perceptible delay before the Title field can be focused and typed into.

test_cases.scenario: Table with a large number of links (50+) does not cause visible rendering lag
test_cases.steps:
1. Create 50 or more links on a single project.
2. Open the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: The table renders all links without visible lag, scroll jank, or browser performance warnings. Pagination handles the display if a page limit is applied.

test_cases.scenario: Links table is clearly laid out on a desktop viewport
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a desktop browser (≥1200px wide).
2. Observe the table columns.
test_cases.expected: The Title and URL columns are clearly visible. Column headers are readable. Row action buttons are accessible and not clipped.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer is fully visible and usable on a desktop browser
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Add Link drawer on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: The drawer slides in from the right. The Title field, URL field, and save/cancel buttons are all fully visible without scrolling.

test_cases.scenario: Edit drawer is pre-populated and fully usable on a desktop browser
test_cases.steps:
1. Click the Edit action on a link row on a desktop browser.
2. Observe the edit drawer.
test_cases.expected: The edit drawer opens with the current values filled in. Both fields and the save button are visible and usable.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal is centred and fully visible on a desktop browser
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Delete action on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: The confirmation modal appears centred on the screen. The link title, confirmation message, and confirm/cancel buttons are all visible without scrolling.

test_cases.scenario: Long link titles are displayed without breaking the table layout on desktop
test_cases.steps:
1. Add a link with a title that is 200 characters long.
2. View it in the Links table on a desktop browser.
test_cases.expected: The title is displayed without overflowing into adjacent columns. The row height adjusts or the text truncates with an ellipsis.

test_cases.scenario: Links tab is reachable and readable on a mobile device
test_cases.steps:
1. Open a project detail page on a mobile device (≤767px).
2. Tap the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: The Links tab is visible in the tab bar (possibly in a scrollable tab row). The links table renders within the viewport without horizontal overflow.

test_cases.scenario: Add Link button is tappable on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a mobile device.
2. Tap the 'Add Link' button.
test_cases.expected: The button registers the tap. The Add Link drawer opens without requiring precise clicking.

test_cases.scenario: Create drawer is usable on mobile — fields and save button are accessible
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Add Link drawer on a mobile device.
2. Tap the Title field and type a title.
3. Tap the URL field and type a URL.
4. Tap the save button.
test_cases.expected: The drawer fills the screen or most of it. Both fields are tappable and the soft keyboard appears on focus. The save button is reachable by scrolling if needed.

test_cases.scenario: URL in the links table is tappable and opens in the mobile browser
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a mobile device.
2. Tap the URL in a table row.
test_cases.expected: The URL opens in a new tab or in the system browser. The original project detail page remains accessible.

test_cases.scenario: Row action buttons (Edit, Delete) are accessible and tappable on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the Links tab on a mobile device with a user who has change permission.
2. Tap the action menu or row actions on a link row.
test_cases.expected: Edit and Delete actions are accessible via a tap-friendly overflow menu or directly on the row. Each action is large enough to tap without mis-tapping.

test_cases.scenario: Delete confirmation modal is readable and dismissible on mobile
test_cases.steps:
1. Tap the Delete action on mobile.
2. Observe the confirmation modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal is fully visible within the mobile viewport. The confirm and cancel buttons are reachable without scrolling or zooming.

test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated GET to the links list API returns 401
test_cases.steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/ without any Authorization header.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 401 Unauthorized is returned. No link data is included in the response.

test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated GET to a single link resource returns 401
test_cases.steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/PROJLNK-1/ without any Authorization header.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 401 Unauthorized is returned.

test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated POST to the links API returns 401
test_cases.steps: 1. Send a POST request to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/ with a valid payload but no Authorization header.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 401 Unauthorized is returned. No link is created.

test_cases.scenario: CSRF token is required for mutating requests from the browser
test_cases.steps: 1. From a browser, attempt a POST to /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/ without including a valid X-CSRFToken header.
test_cases.expected: The API rejects the request. No link is created.

test_cases.scenario: API response does not expose any fields beyond the documented link schema
test_cases.steps:
1. Authenticate and call GET /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/.
2. Inspect each item in the response.
test_cases.expected: Each item contains only: code, project_code, title, url, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by. No internal fields, database IDs, or sensitive metadata are exposed.

test_cases.scenario: A link from Project A cannot be retrieved via Project B's URL namespace
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a link PROJLNK-99 under Project A (PROJ-1).
2. Send GET /api/v1/projects/PROJ-2/links/PROJLNK-99/ as an authenticated user.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 404 Not Found is returned. The link is not accessible outside its owning project's URL namespace.

test_cases.scenario: JavaScript-injected title value is rendered safely and does not execute as a script
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a link with the title: <script>alert('xss')</script>.
2. Open the Links tab.
3. Observe the table row and any drawers that display the title.
test_cases.expected: The title is rendered as plain text. No script is executed. The value is HTML-escaped wherever it appears in the UI.

test_cases.scenario: Links from Project A do not appear when viewing the Links tab on Project B
test_cases.steps:
1. Add links to Project A.
2. Open a different project (Project B) and click the Links tab.
test_cases.expected: Only links belonging to Project B are shown. Project A's links are not visible.

test_cases.scenario: Deleting a project removes all its links without error
test_cases.steps:
1. Add multiple links to a project.
2. Delete the project.
test_cases.expected: All links associated with the deleted project are also removed. No orphaned link records remain in the database.

test_cases.scenario: A link created by one user is visible to all other authenticated users
test_cases.steps:
1. User A creates a link on a project.
2. User B (different session) opens the same project's Links tab.
test_cases.expected: User B sees the link created by User A in the table.

test_cases.scenario: The created_by and updated_by fields in the API response reflect the acting user
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as User A.
2. Create a link on a project.
3. Log in as User B.
4. Edit the link.
5. Retrieve the link via GET.
test_cases.expected: The created_by field shows User A. The updated_by field shows User B.

test_cases.scenario: Requesting links for a non-existent project code returns 404
test_cases.steps: 1. Send GET /api/v1/projects/PROJ-999999/links/ as an authenticated user.
test_cases.expected: HTTP 404 Not Found is returned. No data is returned.

test_cases.scenario: A title with special characters (e.g. ampersand, quotes) is stored and displayed correctly
test_cases.steps:
1. Add a link with title 'Research & Dev — "Phase 1"'.
2. View the link in the table.
3. Open the edit drawer.
test_cases.expected: The title is stored exactly as entered and displayed without HTML entity escaping being visible to the user. The edit drawer shows the original characters.

test_cases.scenario: A title at exactly 200 characters is accepted and stored in full
test_cases.steps:
1. Add a link with a title that is exactly 200 characters long.
2. Save and view the row.
test_cases.expected: The link is created without a validation error. The full 200-character title is stored and retrievable via the API.

test_cases.scenario: API list endpoint returns links in alphabetical title order
test_cases.steps:
1. Add links with titles 'Zebra', 'Alpha', and 'Mango' to a project via the API.
2. Call GET /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/ and inspect the response order.
test_cases.expected: The response data array is ordered: Alpha, Mango, Zebra — alphabetically by title.

test_cases.scenario: A link's audit metadata (created_at, updated_at) is returned in the API response
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a link.
2. Call GET /api/v1/projects/PROJ-1/links/PROJLNK-1/.
3. Inspect the response.
test_cases.expected: The response includes non-null created_at and updated_at timestamps. After an edit, updated_at is later than created_at.

test_cases.scenario: Rapid successive link creations do not cause race conditions or duplicate entries
test_cases.steps: 1. Quickly submit two POST requests for links with different titles to the same project in rapid succession.
test_cases.expected: Both links are created independently and appear in the table. No errors occur. No records are lost or duplicated.
